items.title: Can lemon and hot water kill coronavirus experts bust these popular myths
items.snippet_en: Samayam.com states that the idea of lemon and hot water killing the coronavirus is a misconception and completely false, with no scientific evidence to support such claims circulating on social media.

items.title: False claims that drinking water with lemon can prevent COVID-19 circulate online
items.snippet_en: AFP Fact Check refutes the claim that drinking warm water with lemon protects against the novel coronavirus, stating experts found no proof of its effectiveness in preventing the disease.

The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine states that the acid in lemon juice will not kill coronaviruses in the body, and consuming acidic drinks has no effect on coronavirus infections or their replication.

items.title: The Infodemic: Lemon Juice Won't Cure COVID-19
items.snippet_en: VOANews.com states that the claim that a few drops of lemon juice in the nose will cure COVID-19 is false.

items.title: Lemon Juice Tea Does Not Cure COVID-19 in Israel, or Anywhere Else
items.snippet_en: FactCheck.org debunks the baseless claim that a blend of sodium bicarbonate and lemon juice will "eliminate" the novel coronavirus, with an infectious diseases physician confirming no data supports lemon juice killing a virus.

items.title: Association of natural products use with COVID-19 severity and hospitalization
items.snippet_en: An NIH study found regular consumption of lemon and citrus fruits before infection was associated with reduced COVID-19 severity and hospitalization, but this focuses on consumption's association with severity, not lemon juice destroying the virus.

outputs.notes_en: Multiple sources contradict the claim that drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice will destroy the coronavirus, stating there is no scientific evidence to support it. One study found an association between citrus consumption and reduced COVID-19 severity, but this does not support the claim that lemon juice destroys the virus.
